title: On Group Sufficiency Under Label Bias

problems.title: A fixed marginal channel does not invert score-conditional noise
problems.source_location: Definition 3.4, PDF p.4; Theorem 4.1 Eq.(1), p.5; Appendix A.4 Eq.(10), p.19
claim: The proof uses \(\widetilde\pi(s)=T^\top\pi(s)\), with \(T=\sum_gP(G=g)T^g\), after removing group conditioning.
analysis: Let groups be uniform; two binary scores \(s_a=(1/3,2/3),s_b=(2/3,1/3)\) have \(P(s_a\mid G=0)=3/4\), \(P(s_a\mid G=1)=1/4\). Let \(Y\) be uniform independent of score/group, \(T^0=I\), \(T^1=\begin{pmatrix}3/4&1/4\\0&1\end{pmatrix}\). Noise is generated conditional on \((Y,G)\), all channels are invertible, and even \(Y\perp G\), so the unconditional channel really is the paper’s mixture. True group/marginal posteriors are all \((1/2,1/2)\), gap zero. Noisy marginal posteriors are \((15/32,17/32)\), \((13/32,19/32)\). Applying the fixed marginal inverse gives \((15/28,13/28)\), \((13/28,15/28)\), producing claimed normalized gap \(1/28\), not zero. Actual marginalized channel weights are \(P(G\mid Y,S)\), which need not be constant.
result: The central decomposition is false even in binary classification with every inverse and positive group-score cell. Uniform common channels remain a valid special case; no claim is made that every regularized model becomes less fair.
repair: Use \(\pi(s)=\sum_hP(G=h\mid S=s)((T^h)^\top)^{-1}\widetilde\pi_h(s)\). This follows by total probability and the valid groupwise inverse. If retaining the coordinate metric, condition every posterior vector on the same scalar coordinate before inversion.
problems.existing_correction_status: A proposed correction is retained where stated; independent verification and author adoption remain unestablished.

problems.title: Coordinate-conditioned and full-score sufficiency are different
problems.source_location: Definitions 3.1–3.2, PDF p.4; Proposition 5.1, p.5; Appendix A.4 Eq.(9), p.19; A.7, p.21
claim: The metric conditions class \(k\) on scalar \(S_k\), while the theorem controls conditional independence and information given the full vector \(S\).
analysis: Use uniform groups and score weights \(3/4,1/4\) as above, \(s_a=(1/3,1/6,1/2),s_b=(1/3,1/2,1/6)\). Let label posteriors given these scores be \((3/4,1/8,1/8)\), \((1/4,3/8,3/8)\), independent of group given score, with identity noise. Thus \(I(Y;G\mid S)=0\) and full-vector gap zero. But \(S_1=1/3\) is constant: class-one group probabilities are \(5/8,3/8\), marginal \(1/2\), discrepancy \(1/8\). Other coordinates distinguish the scores, giving coordinate \(p=1\) gap \(1/24>0\), while the stated information upper bound is zero. Binary coordinates determine the full vector, so the explicit binary lemma is not refuted.
result: The literal multiclass metric/guarantee identification fails, including its uniform-noise interpretation. No calibration assumption in the statement excludes this interior-simplex example.
repair: Either use full-vector gap \(D_{g,1}=K^{-1}E[\|\pi_g(S)-\pi(S)\|_1\mid G=g]\), for which Pinsker gives \(\sqrt2\,K^{-1}\sqrt{I/P(G=g)}\), or retain coordinate information \(I_k=I(1_{\{Y=k\}};G\mid S_k)\) and bound the coordinate gap by \[K^{-1}\sum_k\sqrt{I_k/(2P(G=g))}\]. These control different targets.

problems.title: The information-bound constant does not extend unchanged above one
problems.source_location: Proposition 5.1, PDF p.5; Appendix A.7 extension claim, p.21
claim: The \(p=1\) constant \(\sqrt2/K\) and square-root exponent are extended without restriction to the \(p\)-gap.
analysis: At constant score, equal groups, identity noise, take \(K=3\) posteriors \((0.9,0.05,0.05)\), \((0.05,0.9,0.05)\), marginal \((0.475,0.475,0.05)\). Scalar/full conditioning agree. The \(p=2\) normalized gap is \(\sqrt{2(0.425)^2/3}=0.3470110469\); information is \(0.9\log(0.9/0.475)+0.05\log(0.05/0.475)=0.4626073734\). The printed overall bound is \(0.3206269461\), too small.
result: The unrestricted extension is false; the corrected full-vector \(p=1\) proposition survives. Experiments explicitly using \(p=1\) are not refuted by this extension issue.
repair: For full-vector gaps, \(1\le p\le2\) admits factor \[2^{1/p-1/2}K^{-1/p}\sqrt{I/P(G=g)}\]; \(p\ge2\) admits \(K^{-1/p}(I/P(G=g))^{1/p}\). Positive/negative probability-difference masses both equal TV, so \(\|P-Q\|_p^p\le2\,TV^p\); Pinsker and Jensen prove the stated bounds. Coordinate conditioning still needs its separate repair.

problems.title: Inverse-noise concentration cannot be uniform over conditioning
problems.source_location: Lemma A.6, PDF p.23; Eq.(8), p.6
claim: The oracle estimator is noise-inverted, but its radius \[3\sqrt2\log(1/\epsilon)\sqrt{\log(6/\delta)/n}\] has no inverse-channel factor.
analysis: At constant score and uniform groups, let true class-one probabilities be \(3/4,1/4\), so all relevant probabilities exceed \(\epsilon=0.1\). Use symmetric invertible channel \(T_\eta=\begin{pmatrix}1/2+\eta&1/2-\eta\\1/2-\eta&1/2+\eta\end{pmatrix}\), \(\eta=10^{-4}\). The exact oracle summand is \(m\pm d\), \(m=\tfrac12\log(3/4)\), \(d=\log3/(4\eta)\), with plus probability \(q=1/2+\eta/2\). Hence \(\widehat I_n=m+d(2B/n-1)\), \(B\sim\mathrm{Bin}(n,q)\). At \(n=100,\delta=0.05\), claimed radius \(2.1374991968\) passes only \(B=50\); failure is \(1-\binom{100}{50}q^{50}(1-q)^{50}=0.9204108024\), not at most \(0.05\). Distinct channels \(T_\eta,T_{2\eta}\) also give probability-one failure at \(n=1\).
result: The finite-sample guarantee is false. The proof concentrates a different clean-label plug-in variable. Oracle backward correction can remain unbiased; clipping changes bias and does not prove the unclipped theorem.
repair: Let \(M=\max_g\|(T^g)^{-1}\|_\infty\), \(L=\log(1/\epsilon)\). The actual summand has magnitude at most \(ML\), so Hoeffding gives radius \(ML\sqrt{2\log(2/\delta)/n}\). Preserve the group-probability factor when translating it to a sufficiency bound; nearly singular channels can make it uninformative.

problems.title: The shared forward-corrected head need not learn the marginal
problems.source_location: Section 5, Eqs.(6)–(8), PDF p.6; oracle premise in Lemma A.5
claim: The group-agnostic head uses group-specific forward correction, then is treated as the clean marginal posterior.
analysis: At constant score, equal groups and class-one probabilities \(0.8,0.2\), take \(T^0=I\), \(T^1=\begin{pmatrix}.75&.25\\.25&.75\end{pmatrix}\). Required marginal is \(h=0.5\), but population risk is \(R(h)=\tfrac12 CE(.8,h)+\tfrac12 CE(.35,.25+.5h)\). Its derivative at \(0.5\) is exactly \(-0.45\), and its unique strictly convex optimum is approximately \(0.6911801733\). An intercept head represents either constant, so this is neither capacity nor optimization failure. Equal clean group posteriors or identical channels are valid exceptions.
result: The proposed population objective does not generally justify the oracle marginal premise. Conditional unbiasedness with genuine oracle heads remains valid; usefulness of heuristic gradients is not refuted.
repair: Backward-corrected cross entropy satisfies \[E[[(T^G)^{-1}(-\log h(S))]_{\widetilde Y}]=E[-\log h_Y(S)]\], giving the desired representable population minimizer. Its finite-sample variance/negative losses need separate care. Alternatively mix estimated clean group posteriors with score-conditional group weights.

problems.title: Uncentered logits condition on extra information
problems.source_location: Last paragraph, PDF pp.6–7; Algorithm 1, p.7; probability-score target in Definition 3.1
claim: The implemented/stated heads use raw logits, although sufficiency is defined for their softmax probability score.
analysis: Let uniform \(G\) determine logits \(Z=(0,0)\) or \((1,1)\), and label probabilities \(0.8,0.2\). Identity noise meets the assumptions. Score \(S=(0.5,0.5)\) is constant, with probability-score CMI \(0.1927447570\) and normalized gap \(0.3\). Yet \(G\) is determined by \(Z\), so \(I(Y;G\mid Z)=0\). Linear affine log-odds heads represent the two true posteriors, so the ideal logit regularizer can vanish without a capacity defect.
result: Zero logit-conditioned CMI does not certify sufficiency of the reported probability score. A logit target can be intentional, but is a different guarantee.
repair: Use probability scores or centered logits \(Z^\circ=Z-K^{-1}(\mathbf1^\top Z)\mathbf1\). For finite logits, \(Z^\circ_k=\log S_k-K^{-1}\sum_j\log S_j\), so the two representations determine one another and condition on the same information. Other objective/metric issues remain.

problems.title: The default CMI path softmaxes auxiliary outputs twice
problems.source_location: algorithms.py, MI_Forward.calc_loss lines 223–252 and _backward_ce lines 170–185; Eq.(8), PDF p.6
claim: calc_loss first converts head logits to probabilities, then the entropy helper softmaxes those probabilities again.
analysis: With exact marginal head \((0.5,0.5)\), exact group heads \((0.8,0.2)\), \((0.2,0.8)\), equal groups, identity noise and batch counts \(8:2,2:8\), true information is \(0.1927447570\). A second softmax maps \(0.8\) to \(r=e^{.8}/(e^{.8}+e^{.2})=0.6456563062\). The resulting entropy difference is \(\log2+.8\log r+.2\log(1-r)=0.1356592301\). Both values lie within the optional clipping range. Existing MI_Forward2 passes raw logits and avoids this extra transform, but the inspected default/registry chooses MI_Forward.
result: The post-publication default release differs from the displayed entropy estimator. Historical experiment code, learned-head accuracy and model-ranking effect remain unestablished.
repair: Use the existing raw-logit convention consistently for both heads, or a helper explicitly accepting probabilities without another softmax. This local correction does not solve population-head or representation issues.
problems.existing_correction_status: The author repository already contains the corrective raw-logit MI_Forward2 variant; adoption in the inspected default/registry is not established.

problems.title: Inverse-column softmax corrupts identity-channel pseudo-labels
problems.source_location: MC baseline, PDF p.8; algorithms.py, MC._sample_clean_labels lines 833–846; calibration-label path in train.py
claim: The MC baseline softmaxes a column of the inverse channel and samples it as a pseudo-clean label distribution.
analysis: For \(T^g=I_K\), the inverse column is \(e_j\), so the correct observed label is retained only with probability \(e/(e+K-1)\). Expected flips are \(1/(e+1)=0.2689414214\) for binary labels and \(13/(e+13)=0.8270624068\) at \(K=14\), despite zero noise. General inverses need not be stochastic: symmetric \(0.75/0.25\) noise has inverse entries \(1.5,-0.5\). Row normalization does not remove negatives, and softmax supplies no inverse-noise justification.
result: The released baseline uses an altered label process even for noiseless groups. No comparison-ranking change or failure of multicalibration itself is established.
repair: Identity channels must preserve labels. General resampling needs a Bayes posterior proportional to \(\pi_i(x,g)T^g_{ij}\), with an explicitly estimated clean prior/posterior; signed inverse weights can instead correct expectations without pretending to be sampling probabilities. No universal pseudo-label repair is certified.

problems.title: Nonzero noise can preserve a balanced calibrated posterior
problems.source_location: Text immediately following Theorem A.2, PDF p.18
claim: The text infers strictly positive true-label calibration error of the noisy Bayes score whenever noise is nonzero.
analysis: Let \(Y\) be independent of input with probability \(1/2\), and use symmetric channel \(\begin{pmatrix}.8&.2\\.2&.8\end{pmatrix}\), determinant \(0.6\). The noisy Bayes score remains \((.5,.5)\), exactly calibrated to true labels. More generally binary flip rates \(a,b\) give \(q=b+(1-a-b)p\), discrepancy \(|b-(a+b)p|\), zero at the fixed posterior \(p=b/(a+b)\). A reverse-triangle lower bound that may be negative cannot imply strict positivity.
result: The local inevitability statement requires qualification. It does not refute the consistently conditioned reverse-triangle inequality or the possibility that label bias harms calibration.
repair: State positivity only when the score law gives positive mass away from the channel’s fixed posterior; preserve the balanced symmetric-noise exception.
